title: Authentication Flow
description: Build a complete authentication flow with Redux Toolkit, including login, logout, refresh tokens, and protected routes.

data.text: Authentication is the most common real-world feature built on Redux. With Redux Toolkit's `createAsyncThunk` you can model the entire login/logout/refresh flow, track loading and error states, and guard routes based on auth status.

data.title: Never trust the client
data.text: Auth state in Redux is for UX. Always re-validate critical actions on the server. Sensitive tokens should live in httpOnly cookies, not Redux.

data.caption: The auth state machine drives UI feedback and route guards.
data.definition:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Anonymous
  Anonymous --> Authenticating: login(creds)
  Authenticating --> Authenticated: success
  Authenticating --> Anonymous: failure
  Authenticated --> Refreshing: token expired
  Refreshing --> Authenticated: refresh ok
  Refreshing --> Anonymous: refresh failed
  Authenticated --> Anonymous: logout()

data.title: Auth slice with thunks

cards.title: JWT (in memory)
cards.description: Short-lived access token kept in Redux memory, refresh token in httpOnly cookie.
pros: XSS can't read the access token
Easy to revoke by clearing memory
cons: Need silent refresh on tab focus

cards.title: Server sessions
cards.description: Server stores session in DB/Redis, sends Set-Cookie header.

Auth-aware fetch wrapper

terms.definition: Short-lived credential sent with every API request (5–15 min).
Long-lived credential used to mint new access tokens; should be in an httpOnly cookie.
Cookie inaccessible to JavaScript, mitigating XSS token theft.
A wrapper component that redirects unauthenticated users away from protected pages.

data.title: Silent refresh
data.text: Most apps refresh the access token on app boot and on tab focus using `visibilitychange` so users don't see login screens mid-session.

data.title: Build a full auth flow
data.description:
Wire up:
1. A `/login` page with email/password fields.
2. A `RequireAuth` route guard.
3. A `useAuth()` hook that returns `{ user, login, logout, isAuthenticated }`.
4. A 401 handler in your fetch wrapper that auto-logs out.
steps: Store the refresh token in an httpOnly cookie on the server.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Model the full auth lifecycle: idle → loading → authenticated → error
Keep access tokens in memory and refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies
Use route guards to redirect unauthenticated users
Centralize token injection in an auth-aware fetch wrapper
data.takeaway: Redux Toolkit makes complex auth flows manageable and testable.
